title: ICICI Bank's Nifty 50 weight hits all-time high of 9.45%- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: It has now overtaken its previous peak of 9.41% logged in July 2025.   September 04, 2026 / 14:06 IST             ICICI Bank has quietly reached its largest footprint ever in India’s Nifty 50. At the close of September 2, the private sector lender’s weighting in the 50-share Nifty 50 touched an all-time high of 9.45%, as per NSE data. Thus, overtaking its previous peak of 9.41% logged in July 2025. The milestone follows a sharp summer run in which ICICI Bank gained 113 basis points of index share in just three months. After moving sideways between 8.05% and 8.58% across late 2025 and closing May 2026 at 8.32%, the stock steadily outpaced the broader market, climbing to 9.01% in June, 9.22% in July, and topping out at 9.45% in August. Because the Nifty 50 uses free-float market capitalisation, every uptick in the bank’s fully floating share count translates directly into increased index weight. ICICI Bank’s climb has also shrunk the gap between India's two largest private lenders to its narrowest level since the HDFC twins' mega-merger. With HDFC Bank holding a 9.85% weight at the end of August 2026, ICICI Bank (at 9.45%) now trails the top-weighted banking stock by just 40 basis points. A brief stretch of relative outperformance could see ICICI Bank challenge HDFC Bank for the top banking slot in the Nifty 50. A five-fold expansion The bank’s ascent to record weight reflects a multi-year turnaround across two distinct market cycles. During the aftermath of the Global Financial Crisis in March 2009, ICICI Bank made up a modest 1.96% of the Nifty 50. Since that low, its weight in India's premier equity basket has expanded by nearly 4.8 times. Even during the Reserve Bank of India’s asset quality review in 2016-2018, when legacy corporate bad  loans  pulled the bank's index share down to a low of 4.19% in June 2018, the franchise executed a balance sheet cleanup. Over the following eight years, the bank shifted its focus toward retail lending, SME business banking, and technology-driven underwriting, more than doubling its index presence from that trough. Today, at 9.45%, ICICI Bank sits just 55 basis points away from the 10% mark. Commanding double-digit representation in the Nifty 50 is rare, historically achieved only by names such as Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank. Why the Street Stays Bullish The stock maintains a unanimous buy consensus among 42 tracked brokerage analysts. Price targets among foreign brokerages range between Rs 1,700 and Rs 1,935, underpinned by predictable double-digit earnings growth and steady return ratios. Goldman Sachs (Target: Rs 1,935): Goldman Sachs sees ICICI Bank as a core compounder in Indian banking, pointing to consistent Return on Assets (ROA) above 2.2%. The brokerage expects pre-provision operating profits across the private banking sector to rise at a mid-to-high teens pace through FY27–FY29, with ICICI Bank positioned to gain market share without taking on incremental credit risk. Bernstein SocGen (Target: Rs 1,800): Bernstein raised its target following robust quarterly performance, highlighting that the bank’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) profile has stayed benign at around 1.9%. The brokerage noted that the bank's core margin trajectory remains protected as deposit repricing stabilizes, while its low level of unsecured stress provides clear earnings visibility. Jefferies (Target: Rs 1,750): Retaining ICICI Bank as its top sector pick, Jefferies values the standalone bank at 2.3 times its forward book value (adj. P/BV). The brokerage forecasts loan growth compounding at 15% annually through FY29, supported by manageable credit costs in the 40–50 basis point range and Return on Equity (ROE) hovering near 17%. JPMorgan and Nomura (Targets: Rs 1,735 and Rs 1,700): Both desks maintain positive stances, highlighting the bank's liability franchise and digital adoption via its iMobile platform. They note that the stock trades around 16 to 18 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E), a reasonable valuation given its sector-leading risk-adjusted returns. The Passive Flow Advantage Beyond market prestige, the record 9.45% weighting carries practical implications for capital flows. With domestic passive investing continuing to expand (through Nifty 50 exchange-traded funds, mutual fund index schemes, and mandatory equity contributions from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation), capital is deployed strictly in proportion to index weights. At a 9.45% allocation, nearly Rs 9.45 of every Rs 100 entering Nifty 50-linked passive products is automatically deployed into ICICI Bank shares. This steady institutional inflow creates a structural liquidity cushion, reinforcing the bank's market footprint as it approaches the double-digit threshold. Thus, overtaking its previous peak of 9.41% logged in July 2025.

The milestone follows a sharp summer run in which ICICI Bank gained 113 basis points of index share in just three months.

After moving sideways between 8.05% and 8.58% across late 2025 and closing May 2026 at 8.32%, the stock steadily outpaced the broader market, climbing to 9.01% in June, 9.22% in July, and topping out at 9.45% in August. A brief stretch of relative outperformance could see ICICI Bank challenge HDFC Bank for the top banking slot in the Nifty 50.

A five-fold expansion

The bank’s ascent to record weight reflects a multi-year turnaround across two distinct market cycles.

During the aftermath of the Global Financial Crisis in March 2009, ICICI Bank made up a modest 1.96% of the Nifty 50. Since that low, its weight in India's premier equity basket has expanded by nearly 4.8 times.

Even during the Reserve Bank of India’s asset quality review in 2016-2018, when legacy corporate bad loans pulled the bank's index share down to a low of 4.19% in June 2018, the franchise executed a balance sheet cleanup. Over the following eight years, the bank shifted its focus toward retail lending, SME business banking, and technology-driven underwriting, more than doubling its index presence from that trough.

Today, at 9.45%, ICICI Bank sits just 55 basis points away from the 10% mark. Commanding double-digit representation in the Nifty 50 is rare, historically achieved only by names such as Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank.

Why the Street Stays Bullish

The stock maintains a unanimous buy consensus among 42 tracked brokerage analysts. Price targets among foreign brokerages range between Rs 1,700 and Rs 1,935, underpinned by predictable double-digit earnings growth and steady return ratios.

Goldman Sachs (Target: Rs 1,935): Goldman Sachs sees ICICI Bank as a core compounder in Indian banking, pointing to consistent Return on Assets (ROA) above 2.2%. The brokerage expects pre-provision operating profits across the private banking sector to rise at a mid-to-high teens pace through FY27–FY29, with ICICI Bank positioned to gain market share without taking on incremental credit risk.

Bernstein SocGen (Target: Rs 1,800): Bernstein raised its target following robust quarterly performance, highlighting that the bank’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) profile has stayed benign at around 1.9%. The brokerage noted that the bank's core margin trajectory remains protected as deposit repricing stabilizes, while its low level of unsecured stress provides clear earnings visibility.

Jefferies (Target: Rs 1,750): Retaining ICICI Bank as its top sector pick, Jefferies values the standalone bank at 2.3 times its forward book value (adj. P/BV). The brokerage forecasts loan growth compounding at 15% annually through FY29, supported by manageable credit costs in the 40–50 basis point range and Return on Equity (ROE) hovering near 17%.

JPMorgan and Nomura (Targets: Rs 1,735 and Rs 1,700): Both desks maintain positive stances, highlighting the bank's liability franchise and digital adoption via its iMobile platform. They note that the stock trades around 16 to 18 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E), a reasonable valuation given its sector-leading risk-adjusted returns.

The Passive Flow Advantage

Beyond market prestige, the record 9.45% weighting carries practical implications for capital flows.

With domestic passive investing continuing to expand (through Nifty 50 exchange-traded funds, mutual fund index schemes, and mandatory equity contributions from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation), capital is deployed strictly in proportion to index weights.

At a 9.45% allocation, nearly Rs 9.45 of every Rs 100 entering Nifty 50-linked passive products is automatically deployed into ICICI Bank shares. This steady institutional inflow creates a structural liquidity cushion, reinforcing the bank's market footprint as it approaches the double-digit threshold.
